actualProfiles.name: Optimization Methods in AI
actualProfiles.actualContent: Artificial Intelligence is concerned with building intelligent machines that can compute how to act effectively and safely in a wide variety of novel situations. Computer agents operate autonomously, perceive their environment, persist over a prolonged time period, adapt to change, and create and pursue goals. A rational agent is one that acts so as to achieve the best expected outcome. This course aims to provide the student with foundational abilities in: searching in complex and adversarial environment and optimizing by rational agents. Topics include uninformed and informed search in discrete and completely known environments, local and global search methods in unknown and continuous environments, games played in adversarial environments and constraint satisfaction problems. The second meeting of the class each week is entirely devoted to laboratory work where students tackle exercises and demonstrate their work. Projects are undertaken to provide experience of experimental investigations into areas such as graph search, constraint satisfaction, convex optimization, linear and non-linear programming. There are written Midterm and Final exams.

actualProfiles.name: Introduction to Data Science
actualProfiles.actualContent: Data science provides tools for extracting meaningful information from data. In this course, you develop foundational abilities in data visualization as well as data cleaning and manipulation. Next to traditional data coming in the form of tables, we explore non-traditional data types such as spatial data and text data. The course includes much hands -on work with example data sets coming from sciences, social sciences, and arts and humanities. At the end of the course, you carry out your own research project in which you apply your data analysis and visualization skills to answer a research question.

actualProfiles.name: Image Processing & Computer Vision
actualProfiles.actualContent: Image Processing and Computer Vision deals with extracting high-level structural understanding from digital image and video data. As such, it aims to automate the task of the human visual system. In the broadest sense, Image Processing and Computer Vision studies methods for acquiring, processing, analysis, and understanding of image data. The course starts with a concise introduction into cameras, color models, and various image models and representations, but focuses on the processing, analysis, and understanding of image data. Image processing and analysis have many applications, inside as well as outside of robotics. An important application domain is medical imaging, where the goal is to reveal internal structures to diagnose and treat disease. Another application is remote sensing which aims to detect objects on earth. Image processing and analysis study methods that turn images into better images and aim to identify simple features in images. The course considers histograms, point operators, and local, edge, and morphological filters. It covers the Hough transform for detection of lines and curves, detection of corners, shapes and regions, and segmentation. Image understanding concerns the recognition of objects in images. The course introduces feature detection and tracking and object localization, classification, and evaluation. The Image Processing and Computer Vision course offers ample time to practice with the image processing, image analysis, and image understanding methods that are presented.

actualProfiles.name: Mathematical Methods
actualProfiles.actualContent: Mathematics is the language used to grasp understanding of, to explore, and to gain insight in any of the sciences: physics, chemistry, biology, as well as engineering. None of these can be well understood or appreciated without sufficient skills in mathematics. The aim of this introductory course in the mathematics track is to learn basic widely-used mathematical techniques, such as differentiation, various techniques for integration, complex numbers and differential equations. These techniques are put into context in projects related to real situations in the fields of physics, chemistry, biology, economics, sociology, etc. In this course students will continue to construct knowledge on their mathematical bases already founded. Students will solve many problems as homework assignments. Furthermore, two exams will assess the students for their level of understanding and their ability to solve relevant mathematical problems. A lot of class time will be used to solve and discuss textbook problems. 3

actualProfiles.name: Computational & Numerical Methods
actualProfiles.actualContent: Many problems in science and engineering presented in a mathematical format do not have exact analyt- ical solutions; these problems can only be solved numerically. The nature of the mathematical problem dictates the type of numerical algorithm to use; solving an optimization problem requires a different al- gorithm than solving a differential equation. The prerequisite gateway courseMathematical Methods introduces techniques and methods for solving equations in one variable, for finding derivatives of func- tions, or for solving integrals,etc., analytically. This course focuses on the same mathematical concepts but from a numerical and computational perspective. Numerical solutions obtained through some al- gorithm pose the following challenge: what does the output mean? How sensitive is the algorithm to a wrong input? There are examples showing that numerical algorithms can produce completely wrong and unexpected outputs resulting in a disaster. Numerical and computational mathematics is a broad topic; numerous algorithms exist for numerically solving the same mathematical problem. This courses focuses on algorithms for solving equations in one variable. Several algorithms exist for interpolating or extrapolating functions on the basis of a set of sample points of that function. Numerical methods for differentiation, but especially integration form a set of very important numerical algorithms. The course discusses numerous algorithms for solving ordinary differential equations.

actualProfiles.name: Neurobiology
actualProfiles.actualContent: Cognitive neuroscience uses inputs and perspectives from many disciplines, such as psychology, biology, medicine, computer science, and philosophy. In this course, the focus will be on the biology side of neuroscience. As a result, we will focus on evoluti onary pressures on animals in general, resulting in specific behaviors and physiological processes in these animals and ourselves. In this light, you will gain a greater understanding of biorhythms and natural behaviors, and eventually of specific disorders and diseases. Additionally, we will take a look at the use of animals in neuroscientific research, such as rodents, and discuss ethical and welfare implications. We will also familiarize you with experimental techniques in the laboratory, such as cell st aining and using a microscope, and compare the (brain) anatomy of different animal species. This course will familiarize you with concepts and skills required within the discipline of Neurobiology. A selected number of key topics within the field will be discussed, including comparative anatomy, biorhythms, animal models and ethics, and disorders . The course also includes guest lectures and practical work such as labwork, group assignments and student presentations.
actualProfiles.judgment: Real cognitive/neurobiological contribution; not automatically a complete experimental neurotechnology formation or18ECexternalresearchinternship equivalent.

actualProfiles.actualContent: Explores neural mechanisms behind perception and action. Examines how the brain processes sensory information and guides goal‑directed behaviour using methods from cognitive neuroscience and neuropsychology.

actualProfiles.name: Higher Order Functions
actualProfiles.actualContent: This course builds upon the knowledge gained in the introductory course in Cognitive Science. It will deepen your knowledge of neurophysiology and neuroanatomy. Also, your knowledge of experimental approaches in the field of cognitive neuroscience will be enhanced; such that you become able to evaluate research findings and to design your own experiments. A selected number of higher order cognitive processes will be dealt with, including memory, emotion, social cognition, attention, consciousness, decision making and planning. In addition to established knowledge, current research questions will be discussed in depth.

actualProfiles.name: Psycholinguistics
actualProfiles.actualContent: Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.

actualProfiles.name: Introduction to Brain & Behavior
actualProfiles.actualContent: This 100-level course ‘Introduction to Brain & Behavior’ constitutes the Gateway Course for the Cluster Health, Cognition and Behavior: Units ‘Cognitive Science’ and ‘Clinical Psychology’. In this course you will gain foundational knowledge and essential skills that you will need in intermediate and advanced courses of these units. We will look at the various ways in which psychologists and neuroscientists have approached questions such as: Why do people behave the way they do? Can we predict behavior and mental processes in a particular situation, for example after brain damage? Is it possible to change these behaviors and mental processes? How do nature and nurture interact in the development of how we think, feel and behave? Which areas of the brain serve which function, and how do neurons communicate with each other and with the body? We will explore these complex and fascinating topics together from a neuroscientific and psychological perspective, learning about functional brain anatomy on a micro and macro scale, research methodologies and tools in the fields of Cognitive Science and Clinical Psychology, as well as main psychological theories and the relevance of main clinical skills in Psychology. The course will be organized including a combination of different methods of teaching and learning; e.g. interactive lectures, individual and team activities with a collaborative learning methodology, guest lectures, reflective activities, among others. actualProfiles.name: Statistics & Experimental Methods
actualProfiles.actualContent: The course is necessary for students who want to pursue master programs in psychology and adjacent disciplines, as well as research masters in in medical domain. It is highly recommended also for all those who want to be researchers whether in data science, business analytics, market research, political science or sociology. The phenomena investigated by scientists studying humans are usually complex, thus multiple variables must be used to explain them. The theory and application of multivariate statistical models will be discussed. These models can be used to investigate the relations among many variables simultaneously, thus providing an accurate explanation of the subject of interest. The course introduces most used multivariate statistical models such as linear regression, factor analysis, analysis of (co)variance, and logistic regression. Furthermore, attention is paid to non-parametric tests. Practical application: you will learn to apply these models to data. In addition, learn how to deal with problems that occur when statistical models are used. At the end of the course, you will be able to determine which statistical model should be used to investigate different types of research questions. Furthermore, you will be able to execute the corresponding analyses and report results, conforming to APA guidelines.
